sections.content: How many people stayed in Waltham after gaining qualifications?

Waltham is a small town in Yorkshire and The Humber. Waltham does not have its own university.

Waltham has lower levels of deprivation.
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 345 state-school pupils from Waltham who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 160 (46%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 120 (35%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Waltham to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Waltham's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Waltham in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Waltham move to?

Of Waltham's graduates, 95 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 30 of those graduates (32%) were living fairly locally, in the Grimsby travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Waltham's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 60 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 40 of those qualified non-graduates (67%) were living fairly locally, in the Grimsby travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Waltham's GCSE cohort:

  • 45 graduates left Yorkshire and The Humber
